accept: ascending aortic dissection with valve involvement

findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy from chronic hypertension
ST changes suggesting coronary ostium involvement

echoTasks.find: Linear mobile flap in the ascending aorta with true and false lumens in long axis
Dilated root with flap seen in long and short axis plus early diastolic prolapse jet
Flap in the descending aorta with colour flow in both lumens on transoesophageal imaging

auscultation.added: New early diastolic murmur from valve prolapse
auscultation.murmur: Early diastolic decrescendo murmur grade 2 of 4 at the left sternal edge

exam.general: Acute distress with tearing chest pain radiating to the back, sweaty and pale
exam.other: Right radial pulse weaker than the left, blood pressure differs by 20 mmHg between arms
exam.precordium: Hyperdynamic with a diastolic thrill at the base

history.a: Abrupt tearing chest pain radiating to the back 3 hours ago while lifting weight
Known hypertensive for 10 years, irregular tablets, no diabetes
No prior chest surgery, no Marfan features noted
history.q: Prior aortic or connective tissue history

history.a: Pain constant 10 of 10, vomited twice, no relief with rest
Brought by family, consents for emergency surgery discussion

keyPoints: Treat as a surgical emergency with immediate cardiothoracic referral and no delay for extra tests
Control pain and blood pressure with intravenous beta blockade first, adding vasodilators only after rate control
Keep nil by mouth with large bore access, blood grouping, and urine output monitoring
Confirm extent with urgent CT aortography where it does not delay the surgical team
Counsel the family on operative risk and the need for lifelong blood pressure control and imaging follow up
management.model: Immediate surgical referral with heart rate and pressure control, CT confirmation without delay, and family counselling

sources: ACC and AHA guideline on aortic disease, in own words
ASE guidance on emergency aortic imaging, in own words
stem: A 58 year old hypertensive businessman from Hyderabad develops abrupt tearing chest pain radiating to the back. Arm pressures differ and a new diastolic murmur appears.
teaching: Tearing radiation to the back with unequal pulses is dissection until proved otherwise
Any ascending involvement is type A and a surgical emergency by definition
A new diastolic murmur means the dissection has reached the valve
Rate control before vasodilation is the fellow level resuscitation rule
title: Stanford type A aortic dissection with valve involvement
